title: Origins · the wolf and the first dogs
blurb: Where the dog came from: the gray wolf, the landraces that followed people out of Asia, and the breeds that still look like the animal they descend from.

items.d: The wild ancestor of every dog: 30–80 kg, hunting in family packs across Europe, Asia and North America.
Australia's free-living canid, arrived with people thousands of years ago and never fully domesticated.
Central African hunter that barks almost never, cleans itself like a cat and carries a curled tail.
A highland canid named for its rising howl, genetically close to the dingo and the Basenji.
The royal sighthound of the Fertile Crescent: long-legged, feathered and built to course gazelle.
Mountain sighthound from Afghanistan with a long silky coat and an aloof, independent manner.
Large Japanese breed from the north, kept for guarding and hunting, and famously loyal.
Ancient Chinese breed with a lion-like mane, a blue-black tongue and a stubborn, quiet nature.
